skill.name: azure-resource-lookup
skill.description: Find and list Azure resources across subscriptions or resource groups using Azure Resource Graph. Use it for inventory, tag checks, orphaned resources, and read-only discovery.
skill.summary: Query Azure Resource Graph for read-only Azure resource inventory.

content.value_statement: Azure teams often need quick inventory answers across subscriptions without switching tools. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to query Azure Resource Graph and format results.
actual_capabilities: List Azure resources across subscriptions, resource groups, or resource types.
Generate Azure Resource Graph lookup guidance for common inventory questions.
Route web app and App Service listings through Azure Resource Graph.
Find orphaned disks, unused network resources, missing tags, and unhealthy resources.
Prefer dedicated Azure MCP tools when they fully support the requested resource type.
limitations: Requires an authenticated Azure context and sufficient Reader permissions.
Uses Azure Resource Graph, which can have a small data delay.
Does not deploy, modify, or delete Azure resources.
Does not replace cost analysis or non-Azure cloud inventory tools.

use_cases.title: Audit Resource Inventory
use_cases.description: List resources by type, location, subscription, or resource group for planning and cleanup.

use_cases.title: Check Tag Coverage
use_cases.description: Find resources missing required tags and summarize coverage by resource type.

use_cases.title: Investigate Resource State
use_cases.description: Find failed, unhealthy, stopped, or orphaned resources before operational review.

prompt_templates.title: List Web Apps
prompt_templates.prompt: List all Azure web apps in my current subscription. Include name, resource group, location, plan, and state.

prompt_templates.title: Scope a Resource Group
prompt_templates.prompt: Show all resources in resource group <name>. Limit results to key columns and note the subscription used.

prompt_templates.title: Find Cleanup Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Find unattached managed disks and unused public IP addresses across these subscriptions: <ids>. Group results by resource group.

prompt_templates.title: Build Compliance View
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Azure Resource Graph approach to compare required tags Environment and CostCenter across subscriptions. Explain the query plan and result columns.

output_examples.output: Returns a concise table summary of App Service resources with name, kind, resource group, location, service plan, and state.
Shows matching resources, their resource groups, types, locations, and tag coverage context for follow-up governance work.

output_examples.input: What resources do I have in this subscription?
output_examples.output: Summarizes counts by resource type and highlights where a narrower follow-up query would help.

best_practices: Set an explicit subscription or resource group scope before broad inventory queries.
Limit large results and request only the columns needed for the task.
Use dedicated Azure MCP tools when they fully support a single resource type.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to deploy, update, or delete Azure resources.
Do not run tenant-wide inventory without scope or result limits.
Do not use it as a cost optimization replacement.

faq.question: Does this skill change Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for read-only discovery and inventory through Azure Resource Graph.

faq.question: What Azure permissions are needed?
faq.answer: The user needs an authenticated Azure session and Reader access for the target subscriptions or resource groups.

faq.question: Can it query multiple subscriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the subscription IDs or ask the skill to discover available subscriptions first.

faq.question: When should I use a dedicated MCP tool instead?
faq.answer: Use a dedicated tool when it fully supports the requested single resource type, such as virtual machines or storage accounts.

faq.question: Is Azure Resource Graph real time?
faq.answer: It is near real time, but metadata can have a small delay.

faq.question: Can it help with cost analysis?
faq.answer: It can find cleanup candidates, but cost optimization should use a dedicated cost analysis skill or tool.
